summary: This program builds a small list of farmers' market products, prints the whole inventory, then uses a stream pipeline to pick out the organic items sold in summer, order them from cheapest to most expensive, and collect just their names into a list of strings.

lines.text: Comparator supplies the ready-made sorting rules that the stream's sorted step needs.
Collectors provides the recipes for gathering a stream's results back into a normal collection such as a List.
The inventory is declared as the List interface but created as an ArrayList, which is the usual Java habit of programming to the interface.

lines.code: products.add(new MarketProduct("Heirloom Tomatoes", "Sunny Fields Farm", 4.50, "Produce", "Summer", true));
lines.text: Each product is created with its name, vendor, price, category, season, and organic flag in that order, so the argument order must match the constructor exactly.

lines.code: products.add(new MarketProduct("Wildflower Honey", "Bee Kind Apiary", 12.00, "Honey", "Late Summer", true));
lines.text: The season "Late Summer" is deliberately worded differently so you can see that the filter matches any season containing the word "summer".
An enhanced for loop walks the list to print the starting inventory, which gives you a plain-loop version to compare against the stream that follows.
The main method delegates the real work to a named helper, which keeps the pipeline out of main and makes it easy to test or reuse.
Calling stream() turns the list into a pipeline of values that the following steps process one at a time.
The lambda keeps only organic products whose season mentions summer; the null check guards against a missing season, and toLowerCase makes the match ignore capitalization.
comparingDouble builds a comparator from the price getter, so the surviving products come out in ascending price order.
map replaces each MarketProduct with its name, changing the stream's element type from MarketProduct to String.
collect is the terminal operation that actually runs the pipeline and packages the names into a List<String>.
